messages:
arya: quick thought - i'm sketching a "pin handshake" addition to rollout metadata to support tenant-scoped soft pins. rough idea: add `pin.scope` and a small `lease` object so clients can request affinity without global pins. any immediate objections? :thinking:

mike: sounds useful. two concerns: (1) soft vs hard semantics — soft should be best-effort affinity, hard must reserve resources and be accounted for. (2) who enforces expiry/revocation. control-plane-issued leases need revocation APIs + clear observability.

sasha: +1 on lease. also we need deterministic fallback order in the metadata. if tenant pin fails, clients need a canonical fallback sequence (region -> variant -> global) or a clear 409 behavior. otherwise clients will implement inconsistent retries.

oliver: ops note: we should introduce a `probe` flag so clients can check routing without actually consuming a slot. otherwise a flurry of retries could create pin storms. probes should be non-mutating and rate-limited.

mike: implementation proposal: control-plane returns `lease_id` + `issued_by` + `expires_at`. runtime will accept `lease_id` and annotate routing logs with `lease_source`. Revoke flow: mark lease revoked in control plane -> runtime drops affinity at next reclaim window.

arya: here's a small schema sketch i had in mind: ```json
{"pin": {"scope": "tenant|region|global", "type": "soft|hard", "lease": {"id": "uuid", "issued_by": "control-plane", "expires_at": "iso8601", "audit_ref": "str"}, "client_probe": true, "grace_window_ms": "int"}}
```

sasha: bikeshed on field names: `lease` is clearer than `handshake`. add `grace_window_ms` so clients know how long runtime may wait before eviction. for hard pins require `commit_level`: `reserved|best-effort`.

oliver: agree on `commit_level`. for hard pins we must surface quota info: tenants can't reserve unlimited GPUs. metadata should optionally include `reserved_units` when hard pin is requested.

mike: compatibility notes: older clients will ignore extra fields, but older runtimes may not honor `lease`. migration plan: (1) emit telemetry when `lease` fields are ignored, (2) use a capability header `X-Lease-Supported: true/false` on resolve endpoints so clients can opt-in.

arya: good — we should store tenant capabilities in control-plane: `rollout.metadata.capabilities: supports_lease=true|false`. clients can call `/resolve` to check capability before requesting lease.

sasha: storage concern: we can't store full JSON per-tenant per-model in the routing index. suggest compact encoding: `pin_mask` bits + optional `lease_ptr` (pointer to small lease table). index entry stays tiny; full lease payload lives in a secondary store.

oliver: GC note: leases need lifecycle cleanup. define `lease_state` = `active|revoked|expired|orphaned`. runtime periodically reconciles with control-plane; GC is async and must be idempotent. surface metrics: `lease_revocations`, `stale_leases_reclaimed`, `lease_reconcile_latency`.

mike: define `client_probe` semantics: `client_probe=true` -> do not create lease; return candidate routing with `probe_ttl_ms` and `probe_confidence` indicating cache freshness. client then decides whether to request an actual lease.

arya: envisioned client flow: (1) client calls resolve with `pin.scope=tenant&client_probe=true` (2) runtime responds with `lease_supported` header + `probe_confidence` (3) if acceptable, client posts request with `pin.lease.request=true` to obtain lease -> control-plane issues lease -> runtime binds affinity.

sasha: failure modes to document: lease issuance can fail due to quota or race. clients should back off and retry with lower scope or higher fallback priority. document explicit fallback table and retry/backoff guidance.

oliver: auditing: every lease assignment must include `audit_ref` and `origin` (api|console|migration). add `origin` to handshake so customers can trace billing or migration scripts.

mike: also add per-tenant cap `max_lease_ms` to prevent runaway reservations and a config knob `allow_hard_pins` per-tenant. runtime enforces max lease if control-plane issues longer TTLs.

arya: plan: i'll write an RFC with schema, sample flows, migration checklist, and adoption gates. action items: mike -> runtime acceptance tests for `lease_id`; oliver -> GC and metrics proposal; sasha -> compact index encoding and fallback priority table. i'll mark fields experimental and include an auto-expiry of schema keys if adoption < threshold after 6 months.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollout-metadata-probe -> staging (sha: bf1e2d3) :rocket:

mike: +1. one more thought: add `lease_supported` boolean in resolve responses as opt-in header so clients can feature-detect. also add telemetry to track probe->lease conversion rate.

arya: agreed. thanks all, i'll drop the RFC in #architecture tomorrow and tag owners.
